title: Binary Search Tree Iterator II
summary: Implement an iterator over a binary search tree in inorder that supports next, prev, hasNext and hasPrev. The cursor starts before the first element; next moves forward and returns the value, prev moves back and returns the value.
inputFormat: The constructor takes the tree root; methods take no arguments.
outputFormat: next and prev return the value at the new cursor; hasNext and hasPrev return booleans.
edgeRules: The draft says verify valid-call guarantees; the statement's rule for calling next or prev at the ends is not recorded.

examples.label: authored-reference
examples.input: tree with inorder [1,2,3]: next, next, prev, hasPrev, next

factsMissing: Calls to next/prev at the ends (guarantee or behaviour)
questions: Does the statement guarantee that next and prev are called only when hasNext or hasPrev is true?
